primary_source.citation: Pyysalo et al. (2019), LION LBD: a literature-based discovery system for cancer biology

research_basis.adopted_design: LION's default open-discovery configuration uses Jaccard edge weights, minimum path aggregation, and sum accumulation across linking paths.
material_differences: LION uses sentence-level entity co-occurrence over a heterogeneous concept graph; this formula uses binary article-level MeSH descriptor co-occurrence.
LION's retrospective evaluation deletes documents where named A and C co-occur; this experiment retains every article and reports direct A-C counts.
LION's published aggregate results informed the formula choice, so this is a literature-grounded baseline rather than an independent method search.
The BioASQ cases and source counts are known, although no BioASQ metric output has been computed.

graph_contract.article_labels: binary unique descriptor set; duplicate assignments are an error
graph_contract.support: n_x is the number of included articles containing descriptor x
graph_contract.cooccurrence: n_xy is the number of included articles containing both distinct descriptors x and y
graph_contract.eligible_node_set: V_t contains every descriptor x with n_x >= threshold t
graph_contract.eligible_edge: An undirected edge (x,y) exists when x and y are distinct members of V_t and n_xy > 0
graph_contract.candidate_set: For seed A, rank every C in V_t except A, including candidates with a direct A-C edge.
graph_contract.bridge_set: For a candidate C, use every B in V_t except A and C where n_AB > 0 and n_BC > 0.
graph_contract.direct_ac_policy: Never delete A-C articles, never exclude C because n_AC > 0, report n_AC, and do not use n_AC as a separate score feature.

edge_weight.name: article_jaccard
edge_weight.domain: distinct eligible descriptors joined by an eligible edge
edge_weight.zero_policy: A missing edge contributes no path rather than an edge of weight zero.

path_and_candidate_score.candidate_formula: S(A,C) = sum(P(A,B,C) for B in bridge_set(A,C))
path_and_candidate_score.interpretation: A candidate scores highly when A and C have many shared linking descriptors with balanced Jaccard strength on both sides; this is a graph association measurement, not a generated hypothesis.

numeric_reproducibility.edge_weight_evaluation: construct Decimal from integer counts, then divide under the frozen context
numeric_reproducibility.summation: sum path Decimal values in descriptor_ui ascending order under the frozen context
numeric_reproducibility.persisted_score_rounding: quantize once after the full sum using ROUND_HALF_EVEN

revision_rationale.construct: A literature gap candidate should combine indirect A-B-C evidence with relative scarcity of direct A-C literature rather than rank generic association strength alone.
revision_rationale.single_change: Divide the unchanged indirect score by one plus the exact direct A-C article count.
revision_rationale.denominator_choice: The additive one is fixed additive-one smoothing: it keeps zero-direct candidates finite, uses no fitted parameter, and makes every additional direct article monotonically reduce the revised score.
revision_rationale.source_timing: Every case-level direct A-C count was already disclosed by the score-free source audit before the initial formula freeze; the feature is not sourced from held-out metric output.
revision_rationale.anti_tuning_boundary: No case kind, split, ontology relation, target identity, named bridge, development rank, or held-out metric output enters the formula. Held-out identities and source counts were known, as already disclosed. The exponent, additive constant, and functional form may not be tuned after this freeze.
revision_rationale.relation_to_lion: LION's retrospective evaluation removes direct A-C documents. This revision does not claim to reproduce that case-specific graph operation; it uses a simpler article-count penalty and reports the material difference.

graph_contract.candidate_set: For seed A, rank every C in V_t except A, including candidates with a direct A-C edge.
graph_contract.bridge_set: For a candidate C, use every B in V_t except A and C where n_AB > 0 and n_BC > 0.
graph_contract.direct_ac_count: n_AC is the exact number of included articles containing both A and C at the case cutoff; zero when the edge is absent.
graph_contract.direct_article_policy: Retain every A-C article in all support, edge, and bridge counts; use n_AC only through the frozen denominator.

score_contract.indirect_score: I(A,C) = sum(P(A,B,C) for B in bridge_set(A,C))
score_contract.monotonicity: At fixed indirect score, R is non-increasing in integer n_AC and equals I when n_AC is zero.
score_contract.candidate_direct_count_scope: Compute n_AC independently for every eligible candidate in the same cutoff graph; the named target receives no special handling.

numeric_reproducibility.arithmetic: Python decimal.Decimal only for every persisted score; native integer rational bounds may only screen rank comparisons and may not be persisted as scores.
numeric_reproducibility.indirect_evaluation: Evaluate every edge Jaccard from integer counts, take each path minimum, and sum in bridge order under the frozen context.
numeric_reproducibility.direct_penalty_evaluation: After the full indirect sum, construct Decimal(1 + n_AC) from the exact integer and perform one division under the frozen context.
numeric_reproducibility.persisted_score_rounding: quantize once after the direct-penalty division using ROUND_HALF_EVEN

entries.potential_role: A separately pre-registered pilot over the measured secondary corpus after a successor semantics protocol explicitly handles its observed publication-year scope. It may support post-snapshot discovery cases but is not an NLM baseline substitute.
blockers: The acquired payload matches all three published aggregate counts, but its measured publication-year scope does not match the reported post-1949 scope: 280 records are dated 1946-1949. All years are parseable, although 751,238 values are not plain YYYY.

The 448-record balanced audit is consistent with meshMajor containing all assigned descriptors under maintained-current PubMed: 5,201 of 5,296 assignments match all descriptors and 455 match MajorTopicYN=Y headings. It is not population-weighted, period-appropriate, or evidence of corpus completeness.
The original 416-record protocol remains immutable. Its separately named 448-record successor and checksum-pinned bounded result retain every original threshold and contribute zero readiness.

A separate 21-case secondary-snapshot pilot is frozen before endpoint-support measurement or formula selection. Its five LION cases are source-labelled reproduction targets and its sixteen controls remain ontology-generated proposals, not independently validated discovery truth or verified absences.

The score-free full-snapshot audit found all 21 cases source-compatible at the primary minimum support of 10. However, held-out hard control generated-hard-2012-04-d019956-d019960 has target support exactly 10 and is ineligible at sensitivity 20. The frozen rule says an unevaluable sensitivity is not a pass, so this pilot cannot earn its passing label and does not authorize metric work.

A separately named source-informed successor now preserves all 21 cases and replaces the infeasible sensitivity 20 with sensitivity 5 while keeping primary support 10. It discloses every source count seen before freeze, labels held-out cases score-unseen rather than independent, and remains at zero readiness.

V2's initial formula is frozen before development output: article-level MeSH Jaccard edge weights, minimum aggregation along A-B-C paths, and sum accumulation across B. It is literature-grounded in LION's default but differs materially in graph and co-occurrence unit, retains direct A-C articles, and forbids held-out execution before a final formula freeze.

The initial-formula development measurement is complete for all 11 cases at support 10 and 5, with zero held-out cases computed. None of the three source-labelled positives reaches the top 5%, while three of four ontology-generated hard controls do at both supports. The lower-support run changes no target score or bridge count. This is evidence of poor development discrimination and likely structural-proximity confounding, not held-out validation or a successful gap metric.

The single permitted post-development revision is now checksum-frozen before revision output. It keeps the graph and indirect Jaccard-sum-min score unchanged, divides every candidate score by one plus its exact direct A-C count, consumes the full revision budget, and pre-registers a mechanical development pass-or-terminate gate. It uses no case kind, ontology relation, or held-out metric output; held-out identities and source counts were already known. It contributes zero readiness.

The revision development gate failed at both support settings: 1 of 3 source-labelled positives reached the top 5% versus 2 required, 1 of 4 hard controls reached the top 5% versus 0 allowed, and only 1 of 4 distant controls fell below the median versus all 4 required. The first two descriptive counts moved in the intended direction from 0 and 3 under the initial formula, but did not satisfy any separation requirement. The frozen mechanical action is terminate_pilot_before_heldout; zero held-out cases were computed, no further revision is permitted, and readiness remains zero.
The measured secondary corpus is not the complete 21,508,439-record 2013 NLM baseline, and the two totals are not a measured coverage fraction.
Only a 2013 snapshot is relevant here, so it cannot supply the missing 2007, 2011, and 2012 releases.
Using it changes the experimental population and therefore requires a new pre-registration rather than a source-status flip.
entries.next_action: Preserve this BioASQ v2 pilot as a terminal development failure and do not compute its held-out layer. The separately frozen autonomous prospective track does not depend on this historical or human-adjudicated path and cannot inherit a pass from it; this terminated pilot does not authorize an LLM interpretation layer.

adjudication_protocol.purpose: Turn the frozen negative-control proposals into reviewer-ready evidence packets without accepting, rejecting, replacing, or scoring any candidate.

authoring_timing.disclosure: This protocol was written after the terminal BioASQ v2 development result, which reused these proposed controls. It does not claim that its author was blind to those pilot outputs and encodes no candidate-level decision.

reviewer_blinding.requirement: Each decision must be made by a reviewer who has not inspected any lacuna score, rank, ordering, bridge, or BioASQ case output for that candidate.
reviewer_blinding.enforcement_limit: Repository validation can require the attestation and direct public decision link, but cannot prove what a reviewer previously saw.

limitations: PubMed applies maintained indexing and current search translation; these links do not reconstruct the pinned production-year citation baseline.
A zero-result query is not evidence that a relationship is absent from academic literature or from non-academic, craft, practitioner, or indigenous knowledge.
The exact-phrase title/abstract query is a reproducible review lead, not a complete synonym search.
Search result counts are live and are not persisted or presented as measured facts by this artifact.

common_review_checks: Verify both frozen descriptor identities against the pinned scope notes, entry terms, annotations, and tree paths.
Inspect both generated PubMed queries before consulting any lacuna metric output; follow relevant citations and add public evidence links to the decision.
Treat maintained-current PubMed retrieval as a review aid, not period-appropriate historical indexing or proof of absent knowledge.
State whether the proposal fits its intended control construct and identify any ambiguity, polysemy, or domain-specific linkage.
Keep the proposal at zero readiness unless an explicit public decision is later copied into cases.json through the existing validator path.

hard_negative: Substantive adjacency is expected: the shared immediate MeSH parent is the confounder this cohort is designed to test, so relatedness alone is not a rejection reason.
Accept only if the pair is a credible ontology-adjacent or classification-overlap non-discovery control whose high structural proximity should not be interpreted as a hidden discovery.

Reject or defer if either descriptor is ambiguous, the shared-parent relation does not capture their practical relationship, or public evidence supports a meaningful LBD-style discovery claim for the pair.
distant_negative: Cross-branch placement is only a sampling hypothesis; verify that the terms remain substantively distant after reading their scope notes and entry terms.
Accept only if no obvious scientific, clinical, industrial, social, or historical linkage makes the pair an unsuitable unrelated control.
Reject or defer generic, polysemous, culturally contingent, or plausibly related pairs rather than converting a weak search result into an absence claim.

acceptance_requires: a kind-specific rationale addressing every applicable check
at least one public evidence URL beyond the generated query links
preservation of the frozen candidate ID, kind, split, cutoff, and descriptor identities
decision_contract.reject_or_defer_effect: The proposal remains outside cases.json and contributes zero readiness; replacement requires a separately regenerated pre-metric selection record.
decision_contract.validator_limit: Structural validation cannot substitute for expert judgment or verify the truth of a public rationale.

adjudication_protocol.claim_boundary: This is a post-BioASQ, metric-v3-blind review protocol and generated-query contract. It is not human adjudication, evidence of absent knowledge, benchmark readiness, or authorization to run a replacement metric.
